text:
matt: Kicked off an offline trace-driven sim to validate the new queue policy and token-budget target. Using Jan-Feb prod traces (heatmap of seq lengths) — trying to see p95 latency vs per-token cost tradeoffs.

yasmin: Nice. Which simulator config are we running? any KV-cache modeling?

matt: Yes, basic KV cache model included (per-session warmup + prefix cache). Config snapshot:```
queue_policy: admit_by_age
max_hold_ms: 12
max_batch_tokens: 2048
token_budget_target: 512
kv_cache_warmup: 2.5s
sim_mode: trace_replay
```

priya: FYI I pushed an alternate config that biases by sequence length (`admit_by_length`) to the sim bucket for A/B. Link: https://internal/sims/17492 (logs + csv).

alex: Quick summary from perf-bot: p95 latency (baseline) = 145ms, p95 (admit_by_age, budget=512) = 128ms (-12%), cost per 1M tokens = $78 -> $71 (-9%). KV hit ratio moved from 34% -> 37%.

matt: That's promising. Did we see any tail amplification from batching (long sequences blocking short ones)?

perf-bot: Observed queue-starvation events at ~0.6% of requests when `max_hold_ms` <= 8ms; bumping `max_hold_ms` to 12ms reduced starvation to 0.05%.

yasmin: Can you paste the sim histogram for batch sizes? I want to check if huge batches are forming for long-tail sequences.

matt: Pasted below (excerpt):```
batch_size_histogram: {1: 52%, 2: 20%, 4: 12%, 8: 8%, 16+: 8%}
long_seq_batches (>=1024 tokens): 3% of batches, but account for 22% of tokens served.```

priya: Do we have per-model kernel selection differences? i.e., does the kernel picker prefer Winograd vs Fused for short sequences and is that impacting latency?

alex: The sim includes a kernel selection heuristic: choose kernel by (seq_len, batch_size, device_memory_state). For short sequences (<128) it prefers fast small-batch kernels; for large seqs it picks fused kernels. No regression spotted, but we did see a ~4ms overhead for kernel-switch when mixing kernel families in the same driver slot.

yasmin: That kernel-switch cost could explain micro tail. Can the sim gate kernel switching (force single kernel family per slot) to measure impact?

matt: Good idea. I queued a variant: `disable_cross_kernel_switch=true`. Will run overnight.

perf-bot: A/B harness note: we replayed 1.2M requests from traces with sampling weights matching live traffic. A side-by-side eval shows quality/outputs identical (deterministic replay).

priya: Any perf regressions flagged besides the 4ms kernel switch overhead?

alex: One regression worth noting — when token_budget_target dropped below 256, we saw lower KV-hit due to smaller prefix batching, which increased cost per token by ~6%. So target=512 seems sweet spot in this trace set.

matt: Action items: 1) Run `disable_cross_kernel_switch` sim and compare p99 tail. 2) Validate admit_by_age + token_budget=512 in canary (small % of live) and measure KV-hit and latency. 3) Add instrumentation to track kernel-switch events per driver slot.

yasmin: I'll take #3. priya can you own the canary rollout?

priya: Yep, I'll schedule a 1% canary for next Tues with rollback alarms (p95 threshold + KV hit delta).

alex: If the canary mirrors sim (p95 down, cost down, no quality delta), we can roll to 10% and tune autoscaler pop-up thresholds.

matt: Great. Leaving the full sim logs here: https://internal/sims/1749209876/results.csv and a short notebook with graphs. Will post a follow-up once the kernel-switch sim finishes. :thumbsup:
